structured_output.objective: Fix TokenBucket freeze on NTP backward clock jump without breaking RedisStore serialization.

verified_facts.statement: TokenBucket.allow() computes elapsed via time.time(), causing negative delta clamped to 0.0 for 298s after a 5-min NTP backward step.
MemoryStore initializes last_refill_ts with time.time() at line 28, tightly coupling in-memory state to wall clock.
RedisStore already accepts caller-provided elapsed delta in Lua script and passes all 2 Redis tests untouched.

ruled_out_hypotheses.hypothesis: Bug is caused by Redis Lua script TTL expiry race condition
ruled_out_hypotheses.disproof: evt_02 proves test_ntp_backward_jump fails on pure MemoryStore with Redis disabled, and test_redis_store passes 100%.

ruled_out_hypotheses.hypothesis: Floating-point precision loss in refill_rate multiplication
ruled_out_hypotheses.disproof: evt_04 verified refill_rate=1.0 with integer seconds still yields 0.0 refill due to wall-clock delta=-298.0.

open_constraints.description: Switch TokenBucket & MemoryStore local timing to time.monotonic() while keeping optional injectable clock for unit tests.
Preserve RedisStore wire format compatibility (do not serialize process-local monotonic floats into Redis).

recommended_next_steps: Inject clock_fn=time.monotonic into TokenBucket and MemoryStore
Keep RedisStore on server-side Redis TIME / elapsed delta
Run full pytest suite and add regression test for backward + forward clock jump
